note:
Re-stamped during the 2026-09-08 sync. This floor was orphaned before the sync rather than by it -- design-themes was not one of the three repos synced -- and nobody had re-banked it. Only the provenance moved: py_lint.py design-themes --check --scope design-themes reports 2 == baseline against the settled tree.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

STAMP RE-POINTED AT A COMMIT THAT EXISTS, NUMBER UNCHANGED. The floor read UNCHECKED: `cc15c000fb0` is in no design-themes object store, so no ancestry test could even fail honestly and the gate was refusing to answer rather than passing or failing. `py_lint.py design-themes --rule noqa-rationale --count` reads 2 on a clean tree at c77831980, equal to the floor, so only the provenance moves.

The previous note is wrong about which commit was lost, and the error is worth naming because it is what produced an unresolvable stamp. It says the floor "was banked at c7783198014, which design-themes no longer holds" and refreshes the stamp away from it. design-themes holds c77831980 today and it is HEAD: the commit that vanished is the refresh itself, not the thing it was refreshing away from. A stamp taken at an intermediate tip that a later force-push rewrites is exactly the UNCHECKED case §4 describes for suite_lane and tsc_serviceworker.

Standing hazard, unchanged: this repository rebases 19.0-marin onto origin/19.0 and force-pushes, so a stamp here is orphaned by design at the next upstream sync. ORPHANED-BASE after such a sync is expected and is re-measured, not read as a finding. UNCHECKED is not that case and should be, because it means the tree the figure claims to describe cannot be checked out by anyone.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

STAMPED, NOT MOVED. The floor carried no `measured_at` at all, so it was a number nobody could reproduce: the guard that refuses a stamp this branch never had cannot fire on a floor with no stamp, and an unstamped floor may never have been true of any tree. Re-measured on a clean detached worktree at the stamped commit -- python odoo/tooling/lint/py_lint.py design-themes --count -- and it reads 2, equal to the floor. The count does not move; only the stamp does. A sibling floor's stamp is the SIBLING's commit, recorded through `--update --root design-themes` from a clean detached worktree of that checkout, so it resolves in the repository that was actually measured.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

First baseline for this scope. `lint_case.is_core_path` scoped every test_lint gate to the community fork, so this repository's Python was checked by nothing at all; `tooling/lint/py_lint.py` runs the same checkers over any roots and its own CI now holds them here.

The floor lives in the community fork because that is where the gate and every other floor live, scoped by provenance so a run judges only this repository's count. `--mode no-increase`, as the other cross-repo ratchets: an exact floor across a repository boundary would make every fix here red until a matching commit in `odoo` banked it. Growth still fails, and lowering is done by hand from a workspace holding all four checkouts.

Measured 2026-08-25 with `py_lint.py <repo> --count`, under exactly the corpus rules the in-odoo gate applies -- verified by pointing the same tool at `odoo addons`, where it reports every number `ratchet.py --list` holds.
